name: Dusty Blue
lede: Dusty Blue is a soft, greyed mid blue, a descriptive name that fits the faded look of old indigo work clothes.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Dusty blue appears in Ridgway's atlas of 1912, in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 and in the xkcd survey of 2010 [1]. The library swatch is slightly greyer than this one, and its nearest named neighbor is [[steel-blue]], about 3 units away [1]. The xkcd name Off Blue is a near-duplicate [1].

St Clair uses the phrase for the Mao suit, the plain blue workwear that became ubiquitous in China, tied to the story of indigo [2]. Synthetic indigo, financed by BASF and developed by Adolf von Baeyer, moved indigo from a luxury on a par with Tyrian purple to the color of blue-collar workforces [2]. The global denim industry, dominated by classic indigo blue, was worth 54 billion dollars in 2011 [2]. See [[indigo]] and [[denim]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive a color near this swatch appears in 122 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.51 per cent, which is more common than 54 per cent of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s at 1.9 times the expected rate, and in a painting it is an accent 59 per cent of the time [3]. These are photographs of aged paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
